intro: The detective has vanished, leaving only a fiddle with one string retuned and a stack of notes addressed to whoever is clever enough to read them. The Irregulars have taken over the sitting-room, spreading the notes across the floor and pinning some to the curtains, and on the mantelpiece sits his pocket-book, open to a page where every line is a pair of figures in his sharp, sloping hand: 3 and 14, 1 and 7, 6 and 2, the ink still fresh. Wiggins says aloud that the first number is plain enough to see, but nobody has the nerve to say what the second might be counting, so they have begun calling the page the Ledger and leaving offerings of sweets beside it.
echo: In the end, somebody always wants to tell.

puzzles.title: Five Orange Pips
puzzles.flavor: A familiar grid, an unfamiliar alphabet.
hints: A familiar grid puzzle in unfamiliar clothes. Once it's done, are some squares more important than others?
Solve it like a sudoku, then read the numbered squares in order.

puzzles.title: The Final Problem
puzzles.flavor: Each entry picked up a hitchhiker on the way.
hints: Each jumble is almost a word from this round, but with a letter to spare. Which letter, every time?
Rearrange each into a theme word; the spare letters, in order, are the answer.

puzzles.title: Seven Per Cent
puzzles.flavor: Turn the wheel until it talks.

blocks.text: BCPCRM SLDSQHSR OBMCBS HC USH HVWG TOF GC HVS DFWNS WG XIGH CBS KCFR DWDS

hints: Try moving every letter the same distance. How far turns the short words into English?
A Caesar shift: find the one shift that fixes a short word, then apply it everywhere.

puzzles.title: A Study In Scarlet
puzzles.flavor: Three letters to a strip, and a note of how long each word was.
hints: The strips are alphabetised, not in order. The word lengths say where the breaks fall. Which strip could start the sentence?
Chain the strips into one string and split it by the word lengths; the sentence tells you what to submit.

puzzles.title: Three Pipe Problem
puzzles.flavor: One horseman, and a field full of noise.

blocks.text: The knight sets out from e5: Nd7 Nf8 Ng6 Nh4 Ng2 Nf4.

hints: Those are chess moves. Which squares does the piece land on, and what's written there?
Start on the given square, play each move, and read the letter on every square it lands on.

puzzles.title: Elementary
puzzles.flavor: A shopping list for a very small, very specific chemist.
hints: Several of these numbers are bigger than 26, so they can't be letter positions. What else has a number that high?
Atomic numbers: write each element's symbol and run the symbols together into one word.

meta.title: Meta: 221B, Upstairs
hints: Every entry has two numbers. What in this round is numbered, and what could the second number count?
The first number picks a puzzle; the second picks a letter inside its answer.
